name: Super Micro Computer, Inc.
blurb: Super Micro Computer designs and sells high-performance server, storage, and networking solutions built on modular, open-standard architecture, serving customers across the United States, Asia, Europe, and globally. The company has emerged as a key supplier of liquid- and air-cooled AI inference and training servers integrating GPUs from partners such as NVIDIA, alongside its broader portfolio of blade systems (SuperBlade, MicroBlade), multi-node platforms (BigTwin, GrandTwin), and hyperscale/cloud datacenter systems. With trailing-twelve-month revenue of approximately $33.7 billion (+56% YoY), SMCI has scaled rapidly on surging enterprise and hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand. The company employs roughly 6,200 people and has been publicly traded since its March 2007 IPO.
recent: SMCI reported its most recent quarterly earnings on May 5, 2026, with the stock subsequently declining and trading around $32 as of May 13-14, 2026 — roughly half its 52-week high of $62.36, reflecting a market-cap contraction to approximately $19.3 billion. Analyst consensus sits at Hold with a mean price target of $36, implying modest upside from current levels. A recent MSN report flagged near-term selling pressure on the stock, though specific catalyst details were not available in the provided sources.
